native_mirror_before.title: The parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module
native_mirror_before.statement: Assume AC and $I$ bounded below. The standard-class map $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$ identifies the direct-sum K0 of genuine tableau parabolic blocks with the full integral Fock module, with matching multiset degrees and residue Chevalley action of $gl_{I^+}$. For every projective $P$ and finite-length $N$, $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ at $s=1$. In particular $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$; no false standard/simple orthogonality $\langle M_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$ is asserted. The projective, simple and tilting basis identifications are proved separately below.
native_mirror_before.strategy: Use the genuine15 finite-length simple/standard bases and the earlier Casimir standard-flag operator identification. Character injectivity makes the displayed map an isomorphism in each finite block, then direct sums preserve it. The mixed multiplicity theorem gives the actual standard/simple transition matrix. BGG and its inverse imply that P and L are dual at1 under the source Fock pairing: ψ becomes identity at1, since normalized Hecke generators become bar-fixed, so its monomial Gram matrix specializes toI. Additivity of exact Hom(P,−) on a composition series then proves the general Hom pairing; it is P/L, not M/L. No graded lift of category O is used.

references.title: Jonathan Brundan and Alexander Kleshchev, The degenerate analogue of Ariki's categorification theorem, Math. Z. 266 (2010) 877-919 (complete 44-page arXiv article)
references.locator: Section 3.1, Theorem 3.1(i)-(iii) and its proof (printed pp. 21-22): the identification of $[\mathcal O^\Lambda]$ with $F(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ by $[M(A)]\leftrightarrow M_A$, the functor action and the Hom-pairing statement; complete passage read.
